limitations: Adult male mice; Online Methods state two to three months, but Supplementary Table 2 reports mean ages of 14.8 weeks for C57BL/6 and 17.0 weeks for knockout laser-Doppler cohorts. No exact universal age range is admitted. No randomization, blinding, prospective sample-size calculation or exclusions were reported.

Kcnj2 deletion uses constitutive Tek-Cre, not adult-induced capillary-only deletion. Isolated cEC currents and control smooth-muscle currents support endothelial attribution but do not exclude developmental effects or establish restriction to one vascular segment. Identical listed genotyping primer pairs require verification before protocol reproduction.

Whole-cell currents are measured with 60 mM external potassium; this recording solution is distinct from 10 mM focal capillary stimulation, 15 mM cortical superfusion and physiological neural release. Kir2.1/Kcnj2 is the primary molecular identity. Ba2+ also blocks vascular Kir channels outside capillary endothelium.

CaPA is an isolated, pressurized preparation with sealed capillary ends, not normal flowing blood. Diameter, upstream smooth-muscle voltage and in vivo flux come from separate recordings. Membrane-potential recordings use wortmannin to suppress movement. Estimated conduction speed is inferred from distance and onset, not voltage measured along every endothelial cell.

In vivo measurements use acute cranial windows and alpha-chloralose/urethane after isoflurane surgery. RBC flux is cells per second; velocity is distance per time; laser Doppler gives a relative tissue perfusion signal. None is BOLD, oxygen consumption or an exact anatomical network reconstruction.

Peak RBC flux is the maximum one-second bin in an approximately seventeen-second post-stimulus interval relative to about three seconds of baseline. Velocity is sampled in the peak-flux bin, not an independently selected peak. Paired observations and nested capillaries are not independent mice.

The Figure 4 diameter null concerns eighteen capillaries in seven mice; the authors state that sampled measurement sites lacked pericytes. Upstream diameter uses eight paired experiments in seven mice. The local null does not exclude pericyte effects at other segments or prove equivalence.

Whisker responses persist after endothelial Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium has a broader target range and leaves residual perfusion responses. The potassium source during neural activity and the complete intercellular route remain unresolved; potassium ejection bypasses the physiological release step.

Supplementary Figure 5 reports five preparations but paired t statistics with five degrees of freedom; Figure 7 reports group sizes inconsistent with its unpaired-test degrees of freedom. Supplementary Table 1 and Table 2 also reverse control-line sample counts for the flow comparisons. Exact quantitative calibration requires animal-identified measurements and resolution.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence. The selected SK/IK activation protocols do not exclude every calcium-dependent endothelial channel. The LFP control tests selected spectral bands, not complete neural activity, and the TTX potassium experiment does not identify the physiological potassium-releasing cell.

Raw recordings and custom MATLAB LFP software have not been obtained or reproduced. The reporting checklist and main text do not provide a resolved access route. No numerical edge weights, universal minimal carrier counts or independently validated full pathway are assigned.

These are aortic recordings, not brain endothelial voltage recordings.

Retinal SERT tracing uses viral overexpression and terminal transcardial serotonin loading under anesthesia, 6-9 weeks after tamoxifen. Large-artery spreading events require favorable loading and occurred in only two of four controls; single-cell fills occurred in all four mutants. This selected qualitative tracing cannot determine a population conductance or physiological serotonin pathway.

Cx37, Cx40, Cx43 and Cx45 reporter distributions describe vascular segments; expression alone does not measure coupling strength or signal direction. Small-vessel tracer persistence is qualitative. A two-gene arterial deletion does not isolate the function of each isoform or test a selective isoform swap.

Focal visual two-photon imaging measures relative diameter; widefield IOS measures an optical HbT-related response. Neither IOS nor the derived response-propagation speed is a calibrated blood-flow, RBC-velocity, oxygen-use or electrical-conduction measurement. General functional analyses select arteries with baseline diameter greater than 15 micrometers.

Visual activity distance uses normalized, thresholded widefield GCaMP, which is biased toward upper cortical layers. The threshold does not prove absence of deeper or sparse activity. Optogenetic distance instead uses a postmortem ChRmine-expression mask, not simultaneous firing measurements. Histological arterial masks are manually registered and refined, not generated causal geometry.

Motion, pupil and locomotion corrections and signal-selection rules affect the analyzed response. In two-photon processing, selected low-power traces are set to zero by an analysis rule. Linear mixed models account for nesting in functional comparisons; the separate resting-diameter test treats vessels as independent despite nesting within mice.

Optogenetic stimulation uses two-second ChRmine pulse trains and six mice per genotype. The zero-laser condition can retain spontaneous vasomotion and imaging-light opsin activation; it is not an opsin-negative control. Functional imaging days 14-16 after viral injection do not specify a universal post-tamoxifen interval.

Propagation velocity is derived from the inverse slope of optical-response onset time versus position along a selected artery, with onset at ten percent of a sigmoid fit. Figure 5E calls it the slope, whereas Methods specify the inverse. Velocity analysis reports thirty averaged repeats, while the general optogenetic protocol reports ninety per power across sessions; subset selection requires clarification.

Full-screen noise differs from focal circles in spatial coverage and pattern. The comparison does not isolate energetic demand, and oxygen consumption or ATP supply is not measured. Time-to-peak genotype differences depend on distance bin; the farthest optogenetic and full-field bins are nonsignificant, not evidence of equivalence.

Resting microvascular control measures capillary RBC velocity near 100 micrometers depth, not whole-brain perfusion or RBC flux. Tail-cuff systolic/diastolic pressure is a separate systemic control. Nonsignificance in these small cohorts does not demonstrate physiological equivalence.

PMC author-manuscript passages and the author-hosted in-press PDF were read, including main Figures 1-6 and supplementary Figures S5-S7. Selected Methods cover the admitted assays; general cloning/culture methods and remaining supplemental material were not fully audited. Final bibliographic pagination is 5003-5019.e22, whereas the read in-press PDF ends its Methods at e12; version completeness remains unresolved.

Separate statistical/genotyping Tables S1-S2, allele-map files and movies were not obtained or replayed. Raw measurements are available from the authors on request and have not been obtained. The paper identifies code DOI 10.7910/DVN/XRRGRI, but public repository access failed; code files were not inspected or executed. No numerical edge weights or independent experimental reproduction are claimed.

Aortic electrical measurements, retinal tracer spread and awake cortical responses are distinct preparations. Cerebral endothelial voltage is not recorded along the full route. Gap junctions can carry small molecules as well as current; residual vascular responses and alternative routes prevent identification of a unique complete neural-to-vascular mechanism.
